sentence: The NHS says adults aged 19 to 64 should do at least 150 minutes of moderate activity or 75 minutes of vigorous activity a week, plus strength work.
note: NHS: at least 150 minutes moderate or 75 minutes vigorous a week, plus strengthening on at least two days

sentence: The NHS lists at least 150 minutes of moderate activity or 75 minutes of vigorous activity a week for adults aged 19 to 64.
note: NHS adult guidelines

sentence: Strengthening activities for the major muscle groups on at least two days a week are in addition to the aerobic minutes.
note: Strength work does not count toward the aerobic total; at least 2 days a week

sentence: The NHS talk test separates moderate activity, where a person can talk but not sing, from vigorous activity, where only a few words fit between breaths.
note: Talk test descriptions

sentence: The guidance also advises reducing long periods of sitting, and the 2019 update dropped the older rule that activity must come in bouts of at least ten minutes.
note: Reduce time sitting; 2019 revision removed 10-minute minimum

sentence: The NHS says adults aged 19 to 64 should aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate intensity activity a week, or 75 minutes of vigorous intensity activity a week.
note: NHS lists at least 150 minutes of moderate or 75 minutes of vigorous a week

sentence: It also describes a mix of moderate and vigorous activity as a way of reaching the target.
note: Search summary: or a mix; CMO guidance allows shorter durations of very vigorous activity

sentence: The NHS adds that 75 minutes of vigorous activity a week can give similar health benefits to 150 minutes of moderate activity.
note: NHS notes 75 minutes of vigorous gives similar benefits to 150 moderate

sentence: The guidance says activity should be spread across the week, and that all adults should aim to be active every day.
note: NHS: spread exercise across the week; NHS inform: all adults should aim to be physically active every day

sentence: The NHS uses a talk test: at moderate intensity a person can still talk but not sing.
note: NHS talk test: can talk but not sing

sentence: Brisk walking, cycling, dancing, water aerobics and pushing a lawn mower are listed as moderate activities.
note: Moderate: brisk walking, water aerobics, cycling, dancing, doubles tennis, pushing a lawn mower, hiking

sentence: At vigorous intensity breathing becomes hard and fast, and a person cannot say more than a few words without pausing for breath.

sentence: Running, swimming, fast or uphill cycling, skipping and team sports are listed as vigorous activities.
note: Vigorous: running, swimming, cycling fast or uphill, stair climbing, team sports, skipping, aerobics

sentence: The UK Chief Medical Officers' guidelines say very vigorous activity, such as sprinting or stair climbing, can count too, in shorter periods or mixed with other intensities.
note: CMO guidance: very vigorous such as sprinting or stair climbing can count, in shorter durations or mixed

sentence: The NHS says adults should do strengthening activities on at least two days a week, working all the major muscle groups: legs, hips, back, abdomen, chest, shoulders and arms.
note: NHS: strengthening on at least two days a week; all major muscle groups

sentence: Lifting weights, push-ups, sit-ups, heavy gardening such as digging and carrying heavy shopping are given as examples, along with yoga, pilates and tai chi.
note: Strength exercise list

sentence: The NHS says these sessions are needed in addition to the aerobic minutes, because they do not count toward the 150 minutes.
note: Strength work does not count toward aerobic total

sentence: The Chief Medical Officers' guidance adds that any strengthening activity is better than none.
note: CMO guidance: any strengthening activity beats none

sentence: The NHS guidance advises reducing the time spent sitting or lying down, and breaking up long periods of not moving with some activity.

sentence: The Chief Medical Officers' guidance says adults should aim to minimise time spent sitting and, where possible, break up long inactive periods with at least light activity.

sentence: The NHS says exercising even once or twice a week can reduce the risk of heart disease or stroke.
